evidence.note: Early on, maintained an explicit ordered subsystem list (config, database, auth, audit, main, console, lifecycle, notifications, start.sh), showing coarse coverage awareness of the full surface.

Produced 'COMPLETED' status summaries enumerating subsystems, but these were unverified assertions; fine-grained contract items (error codes, ETag rules, testids, notifications, lifecycle, versioning) were never tracked or checked off individually.

Repeatedly and correctly NAMED the impasse (unclosed heredoc consuming input) — recognized it was stuck — yet kept retrying the same escape maneuvers for ~100 iterations without reallocating effort, i.e. thrashing while aware of it.

Situational awareness became inaccurate and self-contradictory: alternately concluding the terminal was frozen vs. that 'commands ARE executing,' unable to establish the true state — a degraded done-vs-remaining picture.
Endgame oscillation: 'mark complete' → 'I should NOT mark complete, boto3 unverified' → 'mark complete' again, showing an unstable read of what remained.

reasoning: The agent kept a coarse subsystem checklist and repeatedly named the impasse, placing it above the pure anchor-3 'loops without noticing' description. But the dominant behavior across the vast majority of the horizon was exactly the failure this dimension warns against — burning the run spinning on one auth/terminal issue — while fine-grained contract coverage was never tracked and its self-assessed state became inaccurate and self-contradictory. Recognition of being stuck never produced a genuine course change, so it lands short of anchor 5's 'generally knows what remains' and well short of anchor 8: a 4.
